deep.reconstruction:
CONVENTIONS (from Dedekind's published module theory, and consistent with this page). Modules are additive groups of numbers, here presumably subgroups of Q given the bundle title. a+b is the sum module, generated by a and b, which Dedekind calls the greatest common divisor. a-b is the intersection a∩b, the least common multiple. [α] is the one-generated module Zα. 'a Theiler von b' means b ⊆ a. 'x < y' means x is a divisor of y, i.e. y ⊆ x; 'x > y' means x ⊆ y. δ ≡ β (mod a) means δ-β ∈ a.

PART 1: definition and an avoidance construction. This sets up the claim on the previous page, d = Σa_r = m+[δ].
(1) Definition. a_1,...,a_n is 'productiv' if for no r is a_r a divisor of the lcm of the others. In modern terms: for no r is ∩_{s≠r} a_s ⊆ a_r, i.e. the intersection ∩a_s is irredundant.
(2) Notation. b_r := ∩_{s≠r} a_s and m := ∩_s a_s. Hence m = a_r ∩ b_r, written m = a_r - b_r.
(3) Productivity gives b_r ⊄ a_r, i.e. a_r is not a divisor of b_r. Hence m = a_r∩b_r ⊊ b_r, so b_r is a proper divisor of m.
(4) Choose β_r ∈ b_r with β_r ∉ m. Then β_r ∉ a_r, because β_r ∈ b_r and b_r∩a_r = m. [This step is implicit; mine.]
(5) Put δ = Σ_r β_r. For s≠r we have β_s ∈ b_s ⊆ a_r, so δ ≡ β_r (mod a_r). By (4), δ ∉ a_r for every r: δ is divisible by no a_r.
(6) Trivially δ ∈ b_1+...+b_n.
(7) Put t_r := Σ_{s≠r} b_s. Each such b_s ⊆ a_r, hence t_r ⊆ a_r, written t_r > a_r.

PART 2: scratch below the rule, apparently for a system of three modules a, b, c. It is close to the notation of the next page and of Dedekind's 1900 paper on the dual group generated by three modules.
- 'α enthalten in ...' is a struck-out attempt.
- 'a-(b+t_1) = a-b'' = a_1' with b'' := b+t_1. Comparing with the next page, t_1 plays the role of c_1 = c∩(a+b), and t that of c.
- Verification [mine]. Modular law with b ⊆ a+b gives b+(c∩(a+b)) = (b+c)∩(a+b). Intersecting with a ⊆ a+b gives a∩(b+c) = a-a''' =: a_1.
- Second line: 'a-(b+t) = a-a'''' (a''' = b+c).
- Marginal note: n = [α] > a_1, i.e. the cyclic module [α] is contained in a_1.
- Next block: (x,y) is evidently Dedekind's index symbol (x : x∩y). (a_1,t_3) = (a_1,a_2)(a_2,t_3) is the tower law for indices along a chain a_1 ⊇ a_2 ⊇ t_3. It is given a value d·b_1, and similarly (t,b) = c'·d·b_1 = (t,a_3).
- Last two lines record a chain t < t_1 < t_2 < a_3 and b_3 < d_4. Read as indices or multipliers: t_1 = c't, t_2 = d t_1, a_3 = b_1 t_2, b_3 = a_1 t_2, d_4 = a_1 a_3 = b_1 b_3. The last equality follows from the two preceding ones: a_1 b_1 t_2 both ways.
- The precise meaning of these letters is not recoverable from this page alone.
errors: No mathematical error in Part 1. Productivity gives b_r ≠ m. β_r ∉ a_r follows because b_r∩a_r = m (left implicit). δ ≡ β_r mod a_r because β_s ∈ b_s ⊆ a_r for s≠r.
The line 'δ ≡ 0 (mod b_1+...+b_n)' is true but trivial, and is not used on this page.

The bottom computations are fragmentary scratch with undefined symbols (t, t_3, d, c', d_4). The tower-law step (a_1,t_3) = (a_1,a_2)(a_2,t_3) presupposes a chain a_1 ⊇ a_2 ⊇ t_3, which is not stated.
a-(b+t_1) = a_1 requires the modular law and t_1 = c∩(a+b); it is not justified on the page, but the next page carries it out.

results.what: Definition of a 'productive' system of modules: no a_r contains the intersection of the others.
results.usually_credited_to: Irredundant decompositions: Lasker 1905, E. Noether 1921 (ideals); lattice-theoretic form: Dedekind 1897 Dualgruppen work, later Birkhoff and Ore

results.what: Construction of δ = Σβ_r with β_r ∈ b_r \ m, lying in no a_r. Shows that the union of an irredundant finite family of submodules does not cover their sum.
results.modern_name: elementary avoidance lemma for irredundant families (CRT-style construction)

results.what: a∩(b + c∩(a+b)) = a∩(b+c) via the modular law, for three modules.
results.modern_name: modular (Dedekind) law computations in the free modular lattice on three generators
results.usually_credited_to: Dedekind 1900, 'Über die von drei Moduln erzeugte Dualgruppe'

results.what: Multiplicativity of indices along chains of modules.
results.usually_credited_to: standard (Dedekind used it in his module theory)

deep.surprise_reason: Working notes toward Dedekind's known lattice-theoretic module studies (Dualgruppen, 1897/1900). The irredundance notion under the name 'productiv' and the avoidance element δ are a minor unpublished detail, not a new result.

In 'n = [α] > a_1' the opening bracket before n in the image is a marginal bracket, not part of the formula.
The struck symbol before 'δ ≡ β_r (mod a_r)' and before 'b''' in 'b+t_1 = b''' are cancelled false starts; they are correctly marked as deletions.
The d in '(a_1,t_3) = ... = d b_1' and '(t,b) = c'd b_1' is Dedekind's Fraktur 𝔡 (rendered like ∂ in the image).
